notes: Single included document (IT guidelines page; the generative-AI guidelines page and Honor Code page carry no additional unit-level rules). Most units address the whole community (actor all). P41 and the P56 framing units are nearest-fit. One UNCOVERED unit: AI-enabled phishing hygiene (no security type exists).

documents.unit: AI Governance Working Group / Information Technology
documents.title: Guidelines and Starting Points (Institutional Guidelines for the Use of Generative AI Tools)
documents.summary: IT-hosted institutional guidelines from the AI Governance Working Group that support experimentation with generative AI. They cover data protection, reviewing AI output, environment, copyright and ethics, and leave teaching and learning rules to faculty.
documents.stance_why: The document states 'guidelines specific to teaching and learning uses are the purview of Bowdoin faculty' and that 'Students are required to abide by faculty guidance for their courses', so it sets no course-level stance itself and hands the decision to faculty.

units.why: The page opens by stating IT 'supports the responsible use and experimentation with generative AI tools', an institution-level stance of support; coded as a framework statement (P56) since it sets purpose rather than a rule for a particular actor.
units.anchor: supports the responsible use and experimentation with generative AI tools

units.why: This passage says the guidelines rest on 'Bowdoin's mission, values, and vision' and name ethical considerations; it states the principles behind the guidelines, so it is a framework/preamble (P56), not a specific ethics rule (P53).
units.anchor: Bowdoin’s mission, values, and vision are the foundation of these guidelines

units.why: The sentence notes the 'AI landscape is evolving rapidly' with 'many ethical considerations'; it names ethical concerns as background, closest to P53.
units.anchor: they also come with many ethical considerations
units.resolution_why: Found only by coder A (B skipped it). The source says AI tools 'come with many ethical considerations'; it is a short rationale statement, so it is kept as an informs unit under P53.

units.why: The guidelines state they 'are shared to support AI understanding, experimentation, and use across the College', defining purpose and scope; coded P56 as an institution-wide framework.
units.anchor: these guidelines are shared to support AI understanding, experimentation, and use across the College
units.frag_start: If you are considering using AI

units.why: 'guidelines specific to teaching and learning uses are the purview of Bowdoin faculty' hands the teaching rule to faculty, so P04 (each instructor sets the rule) rather than a stance type.
units.anchor: guidelines specific to teaching and learning uses are the purview of Bowdoin faculty
units.resolution_why: A coded admin, B coded all. The source sentence 'guidelines specific to teaching and learning uses are the purview of Bowdoin faculty' is a notice to every reader of the page, not an instruction to administrators, so actor is all. Modality informs and type P04 were agreed.

units.why: 'Students are required to abide by faculty guidance for their courses' binds students to the course-level rule set by faculty; chosen P04 over P11 because it concerns who decides rather than non-carry-over.
units.anchor: Students are required to abide by faculty guidance for their courses
units.resolution_why: A coded phase general, B coded course-start. The source says 'Students are required to abide by faculty guidance for their courses' as a standing rule, not tied to a moment such as the first day, so phase is general. Modality must and type P04 were agreed.

units.why: 'you should only enter information available to the general public into generative AI tools' limits what data may be entered, a data-protection rule (P50) because default tool settings are not private.
units.anchor: you should only enter information available to the general public into generative AI tools

units.why: 'Information shared with generative AI tools using default settings is not private' explains the privacy risk behind the data rule; P50 as it states tools store/expose prompts.
units.anchor: Information shared with generative AI tools using default settings is not private
units.frag_start: Information shared with generative AI tools

units.why: 'Exceptions to this requirement can only be made when using AI tools approved and explicitly documented by the Chief Information Officer (CIO)' ties permitted non-public data to vetted tools, matching P50's 'prefer vetted tools'.
units.anchor: AI tools approved and explicitly documented by the Chief Information Officer (CIO)
units.resolution_why: A coded must, B coded may. The source says exceptions to the public-information-only rule 'can only be made when using AI tools approved and explicitly documented by the CIO or CISO'. The sentence grants a narrow permission for vetted tools rather than commanding anything, so modality is may; the restriction is carried by unit_stance restrict (agreed).

units.why: 'You are responsible for any content that you produce or publish that includes AI-generated material' makes the user accountable for submitted/published content, P29 (own what you submit).
units.anchor: You are responsible for any content that you produce or publish that includes AI-generated material
units.frag_start: You are responsible for any content

units.why: 'AI-generated content can be inaccurate, misleading, or entirely fabricated' warns that output may be wrong, which is P31 (verify output), reinforced by the heading 'Review AI content carefully'.
units.anchor: AI-generated content can be inaccurate, misleading, or entirely fabricated

units.why: The same sentence says AI content 'may contain copyrighted material', a copyright caution about AI output (P52) separate from the accuracy warning.
units.anchor: and may contain copyrighted material

units.why: The text directs readers to Canvas resources on 'teaching and learning' with AI; this is support for instructors learning about AI, P63.
units.anchor: Generative AI resources focused on learning and teaching can be found

units.why: 'Faculty should be clear and explicit about their policies on generative AI with the students' tells instructors to state their AI expectations; P09 fits (state expectations) though phrased as should, not a syllabus mandate.
units.anchor: should be clear and explicit about their policies on generative AI with the students

units.why: 'Students are encouraged to ask their instructors for clarification about these policies as needed' is the ask-when-unsure rule, P10.
units.anchor: are encouraged to ask their instructors for clarification about these policies as needed

units.why: The page points students to 'Academic Honor Code and faculty handbook for details', placing AI rules under existing integrity rules; this is a referral, coded P36 weakly because it links AI use to integrity policy.
units.anchor: Review the Academic Honor Code
units.resolution_why: Found only by A. 'Review the Academic Honor Code and faculty handbook for details' is a real directive to students that points AI use to existing integrity rules, so it is kept as P36 with should.

units.why: 'There are AI tools currently available at Bowdoin that are free to access with your bowdoin.edu account' describes college-provided sanctioned tools with free access, P17 (also equity).
units.anchor: AI tools currently available at Bowdoin that are free to access with your bowdoin.edu account
units.frag_start: There are AI tools currently available

units.why: 'tools procured on behalf of the College are reviewed by IT and have the appropriate privacy, accessibility, and security protections' is a vendor/procurement review rule, P65.
units.anchor: tools procured on behalf of the College are reviewed by IT

units.why: 'Let us know if you have procured, are considering procuring, or have any questions about generative AI tools' asks community members to notify IT of AI procurement via a form; part of the same vendor-review process (P65).
units.anchor: Let us know if you have procured, are considering procuring

units.why: IT workshops and LinkedIn Learning self-paced AI courses support people in learning AI; the closest type is P44 (building AI skills), and P63 does not fit as it is faculty-specific.
units.anchor: Artificial Intelligence (AI) Self-paced Training Courses, Linkedin Learning
units.resolution_why: A coded P63 (support faculty), B coded P44. The source lists AI self-paced training courses and IT workshops open to everyone ('Workshops and Self-paced Training'), not faculty-only support, so P44 fits and P63 does not. B's fuller anchor naming the courses is used.

units.why: The heading says to 'Adhere to the College's policies, including those on academic integrity'; this subjects AI use to existing integrity rules, P36.
units.anchor: Adhere to the College’s policies, including those on
units.resolution_why: Found only by A. The heading 'Adhere to the College's policies, including those on academic integrity' binds the whole community to existing policies, so it is kept as a must under P36.

units.why: 'Academic dishonesty, in or out of the classroom, ... constitutes a violation of the Academic Honor Code' classifies dishonesty as a violation handled by the Honor Code, P36 (the sentence does not itself mention AI).
units.anchor: constitutes a violation of the Academic Honor Code
units.resolution_why: A coded actor student, B coded all. The sentence 'Academic dishonesty, in or out of the classroom... constitutes a violation of the Academic Honor Code' is a general classification in a page addressed to the whole community, so actor is all.

units.why: 'Integrity is essential in creating an academic environment dedicated to the development of independent modes of learning' gives a learning rationale for integrity; coded P41 as the nearest type.
units.anchor: development of independent modes of learning, analysis, judgment, and expression

units.why: 'Restricted data should not be used with AI tools' is a prohibition on a data class, a privacy rule P50.
units.anchor: Restricted data should not be used with AI tools
units.resolution_why: A coded unit_stance restrict, B coded prohibit. The source says 'Restricted data should not be used with AI tools': a should-not ban limited to one data class, which narrows AI use rather than banning it generally, so restrict.

units.why: 'Sensitive data should be used with caution' tells users to weigh data sensitivity per the Data Classification Policy; privacy rule P50.
units.anchor: Sensitive data should be used with caution

units.why: 'Follow the data sharing practices and policies that were established by the Data Governance Committee' and contacting the data steward is a data-governance procedure, P50.
units.anchor: Contact the person who stewards the data you are using

units.why: The phishing paragraph says generative AI 'has made it easier for malicious actors to create sophisticated scams' and tells readers to 'Continue to use safe computing best practices and report suspicious messages'. The advice is a should addressed to all about security, which fits no type.
units.anchor: Continue to use safe computing best practices and report suspicious messages
units.uncovered_note: Security hygiene against AI-enabled phishing and scams: keep safe computing practices and report suspicious messages.
units.resolution_why: A coded P53 with informs, B coded UNCOVERED with should. P53 covers ethical, bias, labor and environmental concerns, and phishing is a cybersecurity matter. The sentence includes an instruction ('Continue to use safe computing best practices and report suspicious messages'), so the unit is a should and is UNCOVERED, as B had it.

units.why: 'Please consider the environmental impact of AI models and available alternatives before using these tools' asks users to weigh environmental cost, P53.
units.anchor: Please consider the environmental impact of AI models and available alternatives

units.why: 'Aim to use AI tools and services that prioritize more sustainable models' is environmental guidance, P53.
units.anchor: Aim to use AI tools and services that prioritize more sustainable models

units.why: 'Clarify who holds the rights to content generated by AI tools' concerns ownership of AI output, P52.
units.anchor: Clarify who holds the rights to content generated by AI tools

units.why: 'Ensure that output from AI tools do not infringe on existing copyright' is a copyright duty on AI output, P52.
units.anchor: Ensure that output from AI tools do not infringe on existing copyright
units.resolution_why: A coded unit_stance neutral, B coded restrict. 'Ensure that output from AI tools do not infringe on existing copyright... without permission' limits what AI output may be used, so restrict.

units.why: 'proper attribution or licensing agreements may be required' for output based on copyrighted datasets is a licensing/attribution condition, P52 rather than P24 because it concerns copyright sources, not disclosing AI use.
units.anchor: proper attribution or licensing agreements may be required

units.why: 'Make clear when AI tools are being used in content creation or decision-making processes' requires transparency about AI use, P24 (disclosure), applicable to all community members.
units.anchor: Make clear when AI tools are being used in content creation
units.resolution_why: A coded unit_stance require, B coded permit. 'Make clear when AI tools are being used in content creation or decision-making' obliges disclosure of AI use rather than allowing use, so require.

units.why: 'Monitor and mitigate biases in AI outputs' names bias as a concern users must address, P53 (rather than P31) because it concerns harmful stereotypes.
units.anchor: Monitor and mitigate biases in AI outputs
units.resolution_why: A coded should, B coded must. The source is an unhedged imperative, 'Monitor and mitigate biases in AI outputs', so modality is must.

units.why: 'Confirm that any images or videos generated by AI tools are free from copyright issues' is a copyright duty for AI media, P52.
units.anchor: Confirm that any images or videos generated by AI tools are free from copyright issues
units.frag_start: Confirm that any images or videos
units.resolution_why: A coded should, B coded must. The source is an unhedged imperative, 'Confirm that any images or videos generated by AI tools are free from copyright issues', so modality is must.

units.why: 'Be cautious when using AI to generate or alter images and videos, especially in contexts where misrepresentation could occur' warns about deepfakes, an ethical harm, P53.
units.anchor: Be cautious when using AI to generate or alter images and videos

units.why: 'ensure that personal privacy is respected, and obtain consent where applicable' for AI images of people is a privacy rule, P50.
units.anchor: ensure that personal privacy is respected, and obtain consent where applicable
